title: Anthropic Plans to Price IPO at $83 per Share, Fully Diluted Valuation Reaches $1.5 Trillion

content_html:
On November 18, AI startup Anthropic reportedly priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 per share, above the previously expected range of $70 to $78, and will officially begin trading on the Nasdaq this Thursday under the ticker symbol "ANT".

Based on this offering price, the developer of the Claude large model has a fully diluted valuation of $1.5 trillion, a sharp jump from its $965 billion valuation during its previous private funding round in May this year (which raised $65 billion), though it is still below the $2 trillion target reported several months ago.

Against the backdrop of the current turmoil in the tech sector caused by the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and heightened volatility in AI-related stocks, Anthropic's high-premium offering reflects capital markets' continued optimism about the commercialization prospects of leading generative AI companies.

In terms of ownership structure and subscriptions, strategic partners Amazon and Google hold nearly 15% and nearly 14% of Anthropic, respectively. Meanwhile, tech giants including AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC have agreed to subscribe to $26 billion worth of non-voting shares through a private placement concurrent with the IPO.

In addition, although no single venture capital firm holds more than 5%, early backers such as Sequoia Capital, Singapore sovereign wealth fund GIC, Eric Schmidt (each holding about 1%), and Spark Ventures, the only one with a board seat, have all made substantial gains. Some institutions even plan to invest billions more in the IPO. The S-1 filing also shows that seven co-founders, including CEO Dario Amodei, will each sell nearly 3.4 million shares in the IPO, each cashing out about $282 million.

As an important bellwether in the large model field, Anthropic's first-day and subsequent market performance after listing is expected to establish a new secondary-market valuation benchmark for OpenAI (recently reported to be valued at $1.25 billion and has not yet announced IPO plans) and other leading unlisted AI companies.
